Review · the plain deck · for Friday 25 September

The story holds. Write the ask, give the rail a margin, redraw 04 and 11 — and it’s ready.

One clear story, from “sluggish” to a live build, and the drawings on 07–10 are the best thing in it.

What stands between it and Friday: the ask is still a placeholder, the chapter rail runs into the content on a laptop-sized screen, and two diagrams are drawn in a heavier hand than everything around them. The rest is polish.

The deck as reviewed

1 · The diagrams

Five diagrams, three hands.

Your first ask: bring 04, 06, 11, 12 and 13 into line, somewhat. Each keeps its shape; what changes is the pen.

Where they disagree

Five stroke weights (1, 1.25, 1.5, 2 and 3px), five line colours, three kinds of arrow. Red means four different things. Five label styles, three title sizes, five body sizes, three ways of numbering.

04 and 11 are the outliers — filled bands and chips, heavier lines. 06, 12 and 13 are already close.

One grammar

Borrowed from the drawings.

The drawings on 07–10 already speak one language: hairlines, white, one red. Give the five diagrams the same one — mostly by taking things away.

  1. Line. 1px. Ink for flow and connection; #D7D8D6 for boxes and dividers. The one heavier line: a 2px top rule for a group head.
  2. Dash. Dashed 5/4 means “goes back” or “not yet” — the drawings’ hidden line.
  3. Arrow. One solid 6×8 head, only where work flows (04). Elsewhere, stems with no head.
  4. Box. White, square corners, 1px keyline. No filled bands, no white type on colour.
  5. Type. Labels in the eyebrow style (12px, caps, tracked). Numbers “01”, grey. Titles 18px bold. Body 16px.
  6. Red. Once per diagram, on the thing to look at — the job red does in every drawing. Never numbering, never a fill.
  7. Ground. Diagrams on grey with white boxes; drawings on white. 06 has no boxes and stays white.

Slide 04Before Friday

The loop: hairlines and labels, not filled bands

Wrong
It is drawn in a heavier hand than anything around it: black and red header bands, grey arrows at 1.5px, a 2px loop. And the black and red box borders it asks for never render (a CSS slip), so the bands sit in grey boxes.
Change
Header bands become labels over a hairline — “01 Intake”, the number in grey. Boxes 1px #D7D8D6. Arrows 1px ink with a small head. Red goes only on the two checks (a 2px red top rule on steps 04 and 05, and their red notes) and on the loop, at 1.5px dashed.
Keep
Six boxes in one row, the loop underneath, the note under each step.
Why
the headline says “checked automatically and by a human” — red should point at exactly those two steps.

4 · Story and pace

It hangs together. Three seams show.

Slow → we tried AI → it invented parts, like we did → what else slows us → four fixes → what Apollo is → watch it build → the ask → the payoff. The seams: the diagnosis is split around the fixes, four fixes become three elements, and the ask is unwritten.

Technical — files, the commit reviewed, how things were measured

Reviewed: notes/_DEMO-SLIDES-apollo-2026-09-22-v14-plain.html at commit 57e885b0 (blob c68c6640, identical to the working tree; unchanged after every render in this review). Slide renders: notes/_lanes/297/A/after/, 1440×900 at 2×, taken 21:10–21:11 BST, after the deck’s last write at 21:10:36.

Filed reports: notes/_subreports/2026-09-22-297-R1-art-director-diagrams.md · …-297-R2-typography-alignment.md · …-297-R3-copy-editor.md · …-297-R4-publisher-story-pace.md · conductor: …-297-R-review-conductor.md. No Agent tool was available at this seat, so the four passes ran in sequence at the conductor’s seat and were filed under the four names.

Measured: notes/_lanes/297/R/measure.py → _measure.json. Playwright on the mount (headless Chromium via ensure_env.sh / seat_env.sh), page.goto(file://…), each slide via deckGo(n); computed styles, bounding boxes, word-level line boxes; the rail title’s rect tested against every text line box with 8px clearance (plus a manual read of image and pseudo-element hits on 12 and 16). Viewports 1440×900, 1680×1050, 1920×1080. Drawing line specs read from the canvas source: ink #111 1px, hidden #BDBDBD 1px dashed 5/4, centre #9B9B9B 1px dash-dot 9/3/2/3, red #DA1A00 1px (node 1.4px).

Sketches: notes/_lanes/297/R/sketch_render.py → notes/_lanes/297/R/sketch/P*.png: the proposals injected as CSS and DOM edits at render time only. The SVG sketches in section 1 are drawn by hand in this page.

The 04 slip: #s5x .blk{border-color:var(--black)} and #s5x .red{border-color:var(--accent)} (specificity 0,1,1,0) lose to #s5x .steps li{border:1.5px solid var(--g3)} (0,1,1,1); computed border colour on steps 2, 4 and 5 is rgb(215,216,214).

Rail maths: rail title right edge 166–195px (“THE ASK” … “EVALUATION”), centre at 0.38 × viewport height. Content left = max(6vw, (W − 1120)/2) on standard slides and max(6vw, (W − 1360)/2) on 07–10, so the standard slides clear from ≈1540px wide and the drawing cards from ≈1780px. Fix as rendered: .slide{padding-left:max(6vw,232px)} and the same on #s10map, which sets its own padding shorthand. Hide on the close: add s12 to RAIL.hideOn.

Fonts: the stack is “Univers Next”, “Helvetica Neue”, Helvetica, Arial. At the render seat fc-match gives DejaVu for the first two and Chromium falls to the Helvetica alias (Nimbus Sans / Liberation Sans); the bank’s Univers is present as family “HSBC_MtUnivers_Latin”. Line breaks on the presenting Mac may move by a word.

Estimates: minutes per slide are estimates at spoken pace, not measurements. The demo’s 5 minutes is assumed.

Rulings: his 22:05 words appended to notes/_lanes/297/DAVE-RULINGS-2026-09-22.md. His own copy was taken from that file, notes/_lanes/296/DAVE-RULINGS-2026-09-22.md and notes/_lanes/289/deck/BRIEF-v9-recut.md.
